title: Yakitori
subtitle: Japanese grilled chicken skewers with tare glaze
excerpt: Yakitori are Japanese grilled chicken skewers coated with a sweet soy tare glaze. Traditionally cooked over binchotan charcoal, they work well under a very hot grill or over a gas barbecue. The skewers are basted repeatedly with tare as they cook, building up a thick, glossy coating.
sourceNotes: Yakitori (grilled bird) became a staple of Japanese street food and izakaya culture in the Meiji period (late 19th century). Yakitori-ya restaurants serve grilled skewers of every chicken part: thigh, breast, liver, heart, and skin. The sweet soy tare is the unifying element.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tare keeps in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.

content.text: Soak bamboo skewers in cold water for 30 minutes before grilling or the tips will catch fire. Cut the chicken into bite-sized cubes. The tare glaze is made on the hob: soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar simmered until thick, then applied to the skewers in layers under the grill.

Make the tare: put the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar into a small saucepan over medium heat. Stir until the sugar dissolves, then simmer for 4 to 5 minutes until the mixture has reduced by a third and is slightly syrupy. Remove from the heat.
Thread the chicken and spring onion alternately onto soaked bamboo skewers, about 4 pieces of chicken per skewer. Preheat the grill to its maximum setting.

Grill the skewers for 5 minutes. Turn and grill for 3 more minutes. Brush generously with tare, turn, brush again. Return to the grill for 2 minutes per side until the glaze is sticky and slightly charred at the edges and the chicken is cooked through. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: Glaze burns black before the chicken is cooked
items.fix: Cook the chicken plain for the first 8 minutes, then apply tare only in the final 4 minutes of cooking. The sugar content burns at high heat if applied at the start.

content.text: At an izakaya, yakitori is served in two styles: tare (with glaze, as above) or shio (with just salt). Shio yakitori highlights the chicken's flavour more directly. Season with flaked sea salt and a squeeze of lemon. Chicken livers work particularly well shio-style.
